title: Waydroid starts but eth0 never gets IPv4 address, no DHCP lease, no network connectivity
body:
## Summary

Waydroid starts normally, but Android never gets an IPv4 address on `eth0`, so there is no network connectivity.

This reproduces after:

- full reinitialization
- switching from current images to older images
- downgrading Waydroid from `1.6.2` to `1.6.1` and `1.6.0`

## Environment

- Host OS: Ubuntu 24.04.1
- Kernel: `Linux 6.17.0-20-generic #20~24.04.1-Ubuntu SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Thu Mar 19 01:28:37 UTC 2026 x86_64`
- Architecture: `x86_64`
- Waydroid versions tested: `1.6.2`, `1.6.1`, `1.6.0`
- Current display session: Wayland
- Host uplink: `eno1` ethernet

## What happens

- `waydroid0` is created correctly on the host
- `waydroid0` has `192.168.240.1/24`
- `dnsmasq` starts and binds to `waydroid0`
- `iptables-legacy` has INPUT/FORWARD/MASQUERADE rules for `waydroid0`
- Android `eth0` is `UP`, but never gets an IPv4 address
- `/var/lib/misc/dnsmasq.waydroid0.leases` stays empty
- `ip route` inside Waydroid is empty

## Reproduction

1. Install Waydroid on Ubuntu 24.04.1 x86_64.
2. Start the container and launch the full UI.
3. Check network state inside Waydroid.

## Diagnostics

Host:

```bash
$ ip addr show waydroid0
26: waydroid0: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 1500 qdisc noqueue state UP group default qlen 1000
    link/ether <redacted> brd ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff
    inet 192.168.240.1/24 brd 192.168.240.255 scope global waydroid0
```

```bash
$ nmcli device status
DEVICE      TYPE      STATE            CONNECTION
eno1        ethernet  connected        netplan-eno1
lo          loopback  connected (externally)  lo
lxcbr0      bridge    connected (externally)  lxcbr0
waydroid0   bridge    unmanaged        --
```

```bash
$ sudo iptables-legacy -S INPUT
-P INPUT ACCEPT
-A INPUT -i waydroid0 -p tcp -m tcp --dport 53 -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -i waydroid0 -p udp -m udp --dport 53 -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -i waydroid0 -p tcp -m tcp --dport 67 -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -i waydroid0 -p udp -m udp --dport 67 -j ACCEPT
```

```bash
$ sudo iptables-legacy -S FORWARD
-P FORWARD ACCEPT
-A FORWARD -o waydroid0 -j ACCEPT
-A FORWARD -i waydroid0 -j ACCEPT
```

```bash
$ sudo iptables-legacy -t nat -S
-P PREROUTING ACCEPT
-P INPUT ACCEPT
-P OUTPUT ACCEPT
-P POSTROUTING ACCEPT
-A POSTROUTING -s 192.168.240.0/24 ! -d 192.168.240.0/24 -j MASQUERADE
```

```bash
$ sudo ss -ulpn | grep dnsmasq
UNCONN 0      0      0.0.0.0%waydroid0:67         0.0.0.0:*    users:(("dnsmasq",pid=...,fd=4))
UNCONN 0      0          192.168.240.1:53         0.0.0.0:*    users:(("dnsmasq",pid=...,fd=6))
```

Inside Waydroid:

```bash
$ sudo waydroid shell ip addr
1: lo: <LOOPBACK,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 65536 qdisc noqueue state UNKNOWN group default qlen 1000
2: eth0@if37: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 1500 qdisc noqueue state UP group default qlen 1000
    link/ether <redacted> brd ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff link-netnsid 0
    inet6 <redacted>/64 scope link stable-privacy
```

```bash
$ sudo waydroid shell ip route
# empty
```

```bash
$ sudo cat /var/lib/misc/dnsmasq.waydroid0.leases
# empty
```

`tcpdump` on `waydroid0` captured a DHCP discover at least once:

```text
0.0.0.0.68 > 255.255.255.255.67: BOOTP/DHCP, Request ..., DHCP-Message (53): Discover
```

but no corresponding lease was created and Android still got no IPv4 address.

## Things already tried

- switched from X11 to Wayland
- full Waydroid reinit multiple times
- removed `/var/lib/waydroid`
- tested official current images and older images
- downgraded Waydroid package from `1.6.2` to `1.6.1` and `1.6.0`
- marked `waydroid0` as unmanaged in NetworkManager
- confirmed host forwarding and NAT are enabled
- restarted `waydroid-container` and `waydroid-net.sh`

## Expected result

Waydroid should obtain an IPv4 address on `eth0`, receive a default route via `192.168.240.1`, and have working network connectivity.
